transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-29
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Narang (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood), Maya Chen (Cedar), Arjun Rao (Cedar), Lisa Gomez (Cedar), Dan Ford (Cedar Sec)

Summary:
Quick sign-off on POC acceptance metrics and agreement on exact reporting format for pass/fail. Agreed to run two benchmark waves: baseline on open model and production-like run in Cedar VPC. Deliverables: CSV export, Grafana dashboard link, raw logs, and a rollup PDF with go/no-go verdicts.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria (latency percentiles, throughput, quality thresholds)
- Workload sizing and concurrency profiles
- Benchmark environment and datasets (redacted patient examples + synthetic augmentation)
- Reporting artifacts (columns, dashboards, latency/cost breakdown)
- Timeline and owners
- Security/access requirements (VPC, SOC2 concerns)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan Miller: All right team, thanks for joining. Quick check — everyone can hear me?
[00:03] Maya Chen: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks.
[00:05] Ethan Miller: Cool. The goal for today is to lock the go/no-go thresholds and agree what we hand back as the benchmark report. I don't want us to leave any ambiguity on what 'pass' means.
[00:15] Priya Narang: I'll start with the performance bucket. Our standard POC baseline includes p50, p95, p99 latencies, tokens/sec and concurrent users. For Cedar's routing profile you told us offline you expect lots of short prompts (under 64 tokens) with some longer summaries up to 512. Is that still accurate?
[00:27] Maya Chen: Yeah that's unchanged — about 70% short, 25% mid, 5% long. Critical part is p95 latency, because UX folks said anything above 600 ms feels laggy in their mock.
[00:35] Priya Narang: Great. For acceptance we propose: p95 <= 350 ms in-hosted test (Redwood hosted baseline), p99 <= 700 ms, throughput >= 1200 tokens/sec sustained at target concurrency, and tail behavior no more than 3% timeouts under load. Those are our initial thresholds.
[00:50] Arjun Rao: That p95 threshold seems aggressive given our dataset and encryption overhead — are those numbers for shared-hosted or Dedicated? We expect to run the final benchmark in our VPC.
[00:58] Ethan Miller: Good callout. The thresholds I just outlined are for the hosted baseline run — think of it as the reference. For the VPC run we agreed to a delta allowance: p95 up to 450 ms and p99 up to 900 ms, as long as the quality metrics are met.
[01:12] Lisa Gomez: Can you spell out the quality metrics? Our PMs want reproducible truth labels for the summaries.
[01:17] Priya Narang: Sure. We'll use three quality signals: 1) ROUGE-L F1 against golden labels with threshold >= 0.62, 2) semantic similarity on embeddings, cosine >= 0.84 for high-similarity expectations, and 3) hallucination rate measured by exact-match to flagged fields — must be <= 2.5% on the test set. We'll also provide human-review samples for spot-checking.
[01:36] Maya Chen: Is ROUGE-L robust for our clinical text? We worry about synonyms and paraphrase.
[01:40] Priya Narang: Agreed, so the primary gate will be the embedding similarity metric combined with human review on a 100-sample stratified set. The ROUGE threshold is secondary but helps automate gating.
[01:52] Dan Ford: Security — we need audit logs for every request during the VPC run. Also keys must be customer-managed KMS; can Redwood support that?
[01:58] Luis Ortega: Yes, for Private deployments we do KMS integrations. For the POC we can provision a short-term customer-managed key or use RBAC masked logs. We'll send the security sheet. Note: transcript might show 'Red wood' sometimes, sorry the mic is glitchy.
[02:12] Ethan Miller: Noted. Back to reporting format — Luis, walk us through the artifacts you'll deliver.
[02:15] Luis Ortega: We'll produce: 1) A CSV with per-request rows (timestamp, request_id, prompt_type, token_count, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, model_variant, error_flag), 2) A JSONL export with raw responses and model logits if requested, 3) Grafana dashboard link with prebuilt panels for latency, throughput, error rates, cost breakdown per million tokens, and 4) A summary PDF with pass/fail verdicts and methodology. All links will be in the drive folder I shared (drive.google.com/bench-cedar).
[02:40] Lisa Gomez: For the CSV column names can you provide a schema? Our analytics pipeline expects snake_case.
[02:44] Luis Ortega: Yes — we'll use snake_case and I'll attach the schema (example: request_id, ts_iso, prompt_type, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, status_code).
[02:55] Maya Chen: For the go/no-go rubric, how are we weighting quality vs latency? Our leadership wants quality to be the priority — if we slightly miss p95 but quality is excellent, we might still accept.
[03:05] Priya Narang: We propose a soft gating model: quality has 60% weight, latency 30%, cost 10%. To pass overall you need cumulative score >= 75/100 and no single hard-failure. Hard failures would be: hallucination rate > 5% or data exfiltration/security violations.
[03:22] Arjun Rao: Who adjudicates the human-review samples? We want a neutral reviewer.
[03:25] Ethan Miller: We recommend a three-person panel: one Cedar reviewer, one Redwood reviewer, and one mutually agreed third party (we can suggest a contracted clinical annotator). That panel's decisions become the tie-breaker.
[03:36] Lisa Gomez: For benchmark runs, can Redwood run an A/B between a quantized variant and full precision so we can see cost/perf tradeoffs?
[03:42] Priya Narang: Yes — we'll include two model variants and run matched-load tests. We'll capture cost estimates per million tokens for each variant.
[03:49] Dan Ford: Any concerns about PHI in sample logs?
[03:51] Maya Chen: We'll send redacted examples, but some context is necessary.
[03:55] Luis Ortega: Please mark any PHI and we'll handle it in the VPC. For the hosted baseline we only use anonymized data.
[04:02] Ethan Miller: Timeline recap — baseline run in Redwood hosted environment by 2025-11-01, CSV + dashboard + raw logs shared. Customer to confirm dataset by 2025-11-03. VPC run targeted for week starting 2025-11-10 with final report by 2025-11-14. Does that look right?
[04:18] Maya Chen: Yes.
[04:20] Arjun Rao: Calendar invite for the VPC run kickoff?
[04:22] Ethan Miller: I'll send it right after.
[04:24] Priya Narang: One more detail — error handling thresholds. We log 429s and 5xx separately. For acceptance we want 429s < 0.5% and 5xx < 0.1% across run. If 5xx spikes we'll consider test invalid and re-run after remediation.
[04:40] Lisa Gomez: For reporting we want the CSV plus an aggregated sheet that shows the pass/fail per metric and a final verdict row.
[04:47] Luis Ortega: We'll include both: per-request CSV and an aggregated metrics CSV following the schema in the shared sheet.
[04:52] Ethan Miller: Great. Any outstanding blockers?
[04:55] Dan Ford: Need the security questionnaire answered. Can you share SOC2 and ISO docs?
[04:59] Ethan Miller: Yes — I'll drop the security packet and KMS integration notes right after this call.
[05:05] Maya Chen: Thanks. Small thing: please include cost runbooks — our finance asks for worst-case 99th percentile cost estimate.
[05:10] Priya Narang: We'll include cost simulations for 3 traffic profiles.
[05:15] Ethan Miller: OK we'll wrap there. I'll email the deck, the sheet, and the security packet. Recap of next steps in the calendar invite.
[05:23] Lisa Gomez: Thanks everyone.
[05:25] Ethan Miller: Thanks all.

END TRANSCRIPT
